_about: Epidemiological inputs for the SEIR-GNN, each with its source. Values are copied from the cited publications, not estimated here. See docs/SEIR_DATA_SOURCES.md for context and caveats.

human_infectious_period.note: Phaijoo & Gurung's gamma_h = 0.328833/day gives 3.04 d; Yi et al. cite WHO's 2-7 d and sample 1/gamma ~ N(4.5, 1.25). Liu et al. use 7 d (gamma = 1/week).

extrinsic_incubation.use: vector E -> I, only for the SEIR-SEI arm

source_inconsistencies: Jaffna: stated all-ages 31.3% but its own age groups imply 36.1%
Trincomalee: stated all-ages 54.3% but its own age groups imply 56.5%
seroprevalence_any_serotype_igg.retrieved_via: medRxiv JATS XML and table image (T1.large.jpg); transcription checked by row and column sums

ascertainment_evidence._note: No single Sri Lanka-wide expansion factor exists in the sources found. The evidence spans roughly an order of magnitude, so ascertainment must be a sensitivity parameter, not a fixed constant.

items.what: inapparent : apparent infections, paediatric cohort, Colombo 2008-2010
primary infections per notified case, children <12, Colombo 2008-2009
reported-to-true multiplier used by the SEIR-LSTM paper this model extends
Southeast Asia expansion factor, symptomatic cases per reported case, 2001-2010 (Sri Lanka NOT included)

serotype_timeline.event: DENV-1 dominant in periodic epidemics; DENV-2/DENV-3 background transmission 2003-2006
DENV-2 cosmopolitan genotype, new to Sri Lanka; 39 of 44 positives Dec 2016-Dec 2017 were DENV-2

annual_reported_cases.note: 2017 had 440 deaths; Colombo incidence 1,419 per 100,000, Nuwara Eliya 118 per 100,000.
